<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span>
       <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552117" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552118"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2458" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2459">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Commercial other loans consist of agricultural loans, receivable financing, loans to financial institutions, loans for purchasing or carrying
        securities, overdraft loans, and other commercial purpose loans.&#160; Commercial loans are underwritten based on the borrower&#8217;s ability to service debt from the business&#8217;s underlying cash flows.&#160; As a general practice, we obtain collateral such as
        equipment, or other assets, although such loans may be uncollateralized but guaranteed.&#160; Commercial other loans are primarily based on the identified cash flows of the borrower and secondarily on the underlying collateral provided by the borrower.&#160;
        The cash flows of borrowers, however, may not be as expected and the collateral securing these loans may fluctuate in value.&#160; Most commercial loans are secured by the assets being financed or other business assets such as accounts receivable or
        inventory and may incorporate a personal guarantee; however, some short-term loans may be made on an unsecured basis.&#160; In the case of loans secured by accounts receivable, the availability of funds for the repayment of these loans may be
        substantially dependent on the ability of the borrower to collect amounts due from our customers.&#160; As we underwrite our equipment lease financing in a manner similar to our commercial loan portfolio described below, the risk characteristics for
        this portfolio mirror that of the commercial loan portfolio.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552119" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552120"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2460" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2461">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Residential real estate loans are a mixture of fixed rate and adjustable rate first and second lien residential mortgage loans and also include
        real estate construction loans which are typically for owner-occupied properties.&#160; The terms of the real estate construction loans are generally short-term with permanent financing upon completion.&#160; As a policy, CTBI holds adjustable rate loans and
        sells the majority of our fixed rate first lien mortgage loans into the secondary market with those loans classified as held for sale and not included in loan balances.&#160; Changes in interest rates or market conditions may impact a borrower&#8217;s ability
        to meet contractual principal and interest payments.&#160; Residential real estate loans are secured by real property.&#160; With respect to residential loans that are secured by 1-4 family residences and are generally owner occupied, CTBI generally
        establishes a maximum loan-to-value ratio and requires private mortgage insurance if that ratio is exceeded.&#160; Home equity loans are typically secured by a subordinate interest in 1-4 family residences. Residential construction loans are handled
        through the home mortgage area of the bank.&#160; The repayment ability of the borrower and the maximum loan-to-value ratio are calculated using the normal mortgage lending criteria.&#160; Draws are processed based on percentage of completion stages
        including normal inspection procedures.&#160; Such loans generally convert to term loans after the completion of construction.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552120" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552121"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2461" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2462">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552121" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552122"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2462" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2463">
<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span>
       <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552122" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552123"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2463" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2464">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Home equity lines are primarily revolving adjustable rate credit lines secured by real property.&#160; Changes in interest rates or market
        conditions may impact a borrower&#8217;s ability to meet contractual principal and interest payments.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552123" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552124"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2464" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2465">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552124" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552125"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2465" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2466">
<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span>
       <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552125" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552126"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2466" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2467">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Consumer direct loans are a mixture of fixed rate and adjustable rate products comprised of unsecured loans, consumer revolving credit lines,
        deposit secured loans, and all other consumer purpose loans.&#160; Consumer loans are secured by consumer assets such as automobiles or recreational vehicles.&#160; Some consumer loans are unsecured such as small installment loans and certain lines of
        credit.&#160; Our determination of a borrower&#8217;s ability to repay these loans is primarily dependent on the personal income and credit rating of the borrowers, which can be impacted by economic conditions in their market areas such as unemployment
        levels.&#160; Risk is mitigated by the fact that the loans are of smaller individual amounts and spread over a large number of borrowers.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552126" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552127"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2467" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2468">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552127" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552128"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2468" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2469">
<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span>
       <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552128" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552129"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2469" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2470">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Indirect loans are primarily fixed rate consumer loans secured by automobiles, trucks, vans, and recreational vehicles originated at the
        selling dealership underwritten and purchased by CTBI&#8217;s indirect lending department.&#160; Both new and used products are financed.&#160; Only dealers who have executed dealer agreements with CTBI participate in the indirect lending program.&#160; The indirect
        lending area of the bank is generally responsible for purchasing/funding consumer contracts with new and used automobile dealers.&#160; Dealer loan applications are forwarded to the indirect loan processing area for approval or denial.&#160; Loan approvals
        or denials are based on the creditworthiness and repayment ability of the borrowers, and on the collateral value.&#160; Upon a dealer being funded on an approved loan application and assignment of the retail installment contract to CTB, CTB will have
        limited recourse with the dealer, as set forth in the CTB dealer agreement.&#160; On occasion, the dealer will execute a separate, full recourse agreement with CTB to obtain customer financing.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552129" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552130"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2470" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2471">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552130" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552131"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2471" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2472">
<div><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span>
       <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552131" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552132"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2472" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2473">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552132" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552133"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2473" continuedAt="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2474">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">CTBI utilizes discounted cash flow loss rate methodologies for all loan segments.&#160; Within the discount cash flow calculation, an effective yield of the instrument is
        calculated, net of the impacts of prepayment assumptions, and the instrument expected cash flows.&#160;&#160; The expected cash flows were modeled considering probability of default and segment-specific loss given default (&#8220;LGD&#8221;) risk factors, utilizing the
        software&#8217;s proprietary database of financial institutions&#8217; filings, evaluated first by geography and asset size and then with the utilization of standard deviations, to assure relevance to CTBI&#8217;s loan segments along with CTBI&#8217;s own loss history.&#160;
        Cash flows are then discounted at that effective yield to produce an instrument-level net present value (&#8220;NPV&#8221;) of expected cash flows.&#160; An ACL is established for the difference between the instrument&#8217;s NPV and amortized cost basis.&#160; Any changes in
        NPV between periods is recorded as provision for credit losses.&#160; The modeling of expected prepayment speeds, curtailment rates, and time to recovery are based on historical internal data and adjusted, if necessary, based on the reasonable and
        supportable forecast of economic conditions.&#160; Management incorporates qualitative factors to loss estimates used to derive CTBI&#8217;s total ACL including delinquency trends, current economic conditions and trends, strength of supervision and
        administration of the loan portfolio, levels of underperforming loans, underwriting exceptions, and industry concentrations.&#160; Forecast factors include gross domestic product, light weight vehicle sales, and the consumer price index. Management
        continually reevaluates the other subjective factors included in our ACL analysis.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552133" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552134"><ix:continuation id="Text_c6c3083bbce647bb9e51d32bdb9e4f2474">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Loans Held for Sale </span><span style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#8211;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Mortgage loans originated and intended for sale in the secondary market are carried at the lower of cost or fair value.&#160;
        Changes in fair value and net unrealized losses, if any, are recognized by charges to income.&#160; Gains and losses on loan sales are recorded in noninterest income.&#160; Mortgage loans held for sale were $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LoansReceivableHeldForSaleNetNotPartOfDisposalGroup" id="Fact_53b0d2a61eb14e838f93498d7bba6a44" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LoansReceivableHeldForSaleNetNotPartOfDisposalGroup" id="Fact_0422731a91694f408f7eeaa35677639c" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.2</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million for each of the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.</span></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552140" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552141"><ix:continuation id="Text_25a51f0d0c4a43cb8de5b1dedf9d78b21">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Mortgage Banking Derivatives</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &#8211; At December 31, 2025, we had mortgage loans in the process of origination totaling $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:MortgageLoansAndLeasesReceivableLoansInProcess" id="Fact_8183a351c38c411bac80edd2a70eba7f" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million which
        are intended for sale to investors in the secondary market.&#160; These forward sale commitments are on an individual loan basis that CTBI originates as part of our mortgage banking activities and are derivatives at fair value with changes in fair value
        recognized in earnings.&#160; CTBI acquires purchase agreements from secondary market buyers prior to closing these loans.&#160; We then deliver the closed loan to the buyer, typically within 30 days of closing.&#160; These purchase agreements are acquired to
        reduce market risk on mortgage loans in the process of origination and mortgage loans held for sale, since CTBI is exposed to interest rate risk during the period between issuing a loan commitment and the sale of the loan into the secondary
        market.&#160; There were <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:MortgageLoansAndLeasesReceivableLoansInProcess" id="Fact_102bb99b16284f0f8d82ccdcb3c37a1d" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> mortgage loans in the process of origination at December 31, 2024.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552142" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552143"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_1487fd85a3044e7f9de9b7b27a7f230a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_6cd57c73a0e24a67abdbbc3a281653281">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Premises and Equipment</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &#8211; Premises and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Premises and equipment are evaluated for impairment on a quarterly basis.</span> <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span> </div>

<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552145" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552146"><ix:continuation id="Text_6cd57c73a0e24a67abdbbc3a281653283">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Depreciation and amortization are computed primarily using the straight-line method. Estimated useful lives range up to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="Fact_23f2af6d53a746dbb2db6a9eee788970" contextRef="c20251231_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_BuildingMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">40 years</ix:nonNumeric> for buildings, <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="Fact_12cabac9211143b296aff649a31b2c80" contextRef="c20251231_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="Fact_8715670ecef8442bb4d5b8858a6615f9" contextRef="c20251231_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">10 years</ix:nonNumeric> for furniture, fixtures, and equipment, and up to the lease term for leasehold improvements.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552146" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552147">
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-weight: bold;"><span style="font-weight: bold;"> <br/>
        </span></span></div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552147" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552148"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_688d6c1558d548f9b6af6b8980c52d1b" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;"><span style="font-weight: bold;">Leases</span> &#8211;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;CTBI does not record leases on the consolidated balance sheets that are classified as short term (less than one year).&#160; A right-of-use asset and a lease liability are recorded for all leases
        with terms longer than 12 months.&#160; The right-of-use asset represents the right to use the asset under lease for the lease term, and the lease liability represents the contractual obligation to make lease payments.&#160; The right-of-use asset is tested
        for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value might not be recoverable.&#160; Leases are classified as either finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern of expense recognition in the
        consolidated income statement.&#160; A lease is treated as a sale if it transfers all of the risks and rewards, as well as control of the underlying asset, to the lessee.&#160; If risks and rewards are conveyed without the transfer of control, the lease is
        treated as a financing.&#160; If the lessor does not convey risks and rewards or control, an operating lease results.&#160; Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized at lease commencement based on the present value of the remaining lease
        payments using a discount rate that represents our incremental borrowing rate, on a collateralized basis, over a similar term at the lease commencement date and may be re-measured for certain modifications or the company&#8217;s exercise of options
        (renewal, extension, or termination) under the lease.&#160; Right-of-use assets are further adjusted for prepaid rent, lease incentives, and initial direct costs, if any.&#160; CTBI does not separate lease and non-lease components and instead elects to
        account for them as a single lease component.&#160; Expenses are recognized through occupancy expense.</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Federal Home Loan Bank and Federal Reserve Stock </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#8211; CTB is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;) system. Members are required to own a certain amount of stock based on the level of borrowings and other factors and may invest
        additional amounts. FHLB stock is carried at cost, classified as a restricted security, and periodically evaluated for impairment based on the ultimate recovery par value.&#160; Both cash and stock dividends are reported as income.</span> </div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552161" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552162"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsServicingOfFinancialAssetsPolicy" id="Text_8b28db74350d458aa1720359b296f06d" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_bf5e8d69621449508aaea07fbdd684471">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Mortgage Servicing Rights &#8211;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;Mortgage servicing rights (&#8220;MSRs&#8221;) are carried at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in loan related fees.&#160; MSRs are valued using Level 3 inputs.&#160; The fair value is determined quarterly based on an
          independent third-party valuation using a discounted cash flow analysis and calculated using a computer pricing model.&#160; The system used in this evaluation, Compass Point, attempts to quantify loan level idiosyncratic risk by calculating a risk
          derived value.&#160; As a result, each loan&#8217;s unique characteristics determine the valuation assumptions ascribed to that loan.&#160; Additionally, the computer valuation is based on key economic assumptions including the prepayment speeds of the
          underlying loans generated using the Andrew Davidson Prepayment Model, FHLMC/FNMA guidelines, the weighted-average life of the loan, the discount rate, the weighted-average coupon, and the weighted-average default rate, as applicable.&#160; Along with
          the gains received from the sale of loans, fees are received for servicing loans.&#160; These fees include late fees, ancillary fees, and monthly servicing fees, which are recorded in noninterest income.&#160; Costs of servicing loans are charged to
          expense as incurred.&#160; Changes in fair value of the MSRs are reported as an increase or decrease to loan related fees. </span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Mortgage loans serviced for others are not included in the accompanying balance
          sheets.&#160; Loans serviced for the benefit of others (primarily FHLMC) totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:LoanServiceForBenefitOfOthers" id="Fact_3af7724965d1415a8140d9b06bbeb690" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">612</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:LoanServiceForBenefitOfOthers" id="Fact_4a0c31ce6351409d98c257ca8418500f" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">667</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:LoanServiceForBenefitOfOthers" id="Fact_8ac5d50a2b7547349bbad73d7d3bc34b" contextRef="c20231231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">725</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2025, 2024, and
          2023, respectively.&#160; Servicing loans for others generally consist of collecting mortgage payments, maintaining escrow accounts, disbursing payments to investors, and processing foreclosures.&#160; Custodial escrow balances maintained in connection
          with the foregoing loan servicing, and included in demand deposits, were approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:CustodianEscrowBalance" id="Fact_9d6986637f9c4c7e8cfdfe610e59b72f" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:CustodianEscrowBalance" id="Fact_47a82da7957644499e1d2f95a1a02fe9" contextRef="c20241231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:CustodianEscrowBalance" id="Fact_95b1766b9da149b7a8d344c783c98b2f" contextRef="c20231231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million at
          December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.</span></div>

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-weight: bold;">Other Real Estate Owned</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &#8211;&#160;Our other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) consists entirely of foreclosed properties.&#160; When foreclosed properties are acquired, appraisals are obtained and the properties are booked at the current fair value less expected
        sales costs.&#160; Additionally, periodic updated appraisals are obtained on unsold foreclosed properties.&#160; When an updated appraisal reflects a fair value below the current book value, a charge is booked to current earnings to reduce the property to
        its new fair value less expected sales costs.&#160; Our policy for determining the frequency of periodic reviews is based upon consideration of the specific properties and the known or perceived market fluctuations in a particular market and is
        typically between&#160;<ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedTypicalFrequencyOfPeriodReviews" id="Fact_5702f69787544f9bbeeadbca03fd8d2a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> and&#160;<ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedTypicalFrequencyOfPeriodReviews" id="Fact_f12519970f144afead3319f40e64a440" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">18</ix:nonNumeric>
        months but generally not more than&#160;<ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedFrequencyOfPeriodicReviews" id="Fact_81b71f087c714dbcac79cd16292bc9e0" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">24</ix:nonNumeric> months.&#160; All revenues and expenses related to the carrying of OREO are recognized through the
        income statement.&#160; OREO revenues are included in other noninterest income, and OREO expenses are included in other real estate owned provision and expense. <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span><br/>
      </span> <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552170" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552171"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsTransfersOfFinancialAssetsPolicy" id="Text_5dad409a4a294a0e91adc07e6cbaac3b" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_33bf1460a4724357a6958315d8a4d93a1">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552171" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552172"><ix:continuation id="Text_33bf1460a4724357a6958315d8a4d93a1">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Transfers of Financial Assets </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#8211;<span style="font-weight: bold;">&#160;</span>Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales, when control over the assets has been surrendered.&#160; Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered
        when (i) the assets have been isolated from CTBI&#8212;put presumptively beyond the reach of the transferor and its creditors, even in bankruptcy or other receivership, (ii) the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from
        taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and (iii) CTBI does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity or the ability to
        unilaterally cause the holder to return specific assets.&#160; If a transfer of financial assets does not meet all criteria for sale accounting, including circumstances in which the Bank retains effective control through a repurchase agreement or
        similar contractual arrangement, the transfer is accounted for as a secured borrowing.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552175" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552176"><ix:continuation id="Text_4142c16dfb794a72a49554c95a1adfba1">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Estimated Credit Losses on Off-Balance Sheet Credit Exposures Recognized as Other Liabilities</span> </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#8211;</span><span style="font-weight: bold; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span><span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">CTBI estimates expected credit losses over the contractual period in which it has exposure to credit risk via a contractual obligation to extend credit, unless that
        obligation is unconditionally cancellable by CTBI.&#160; The ACL on off-balance sheet credit exposures recognized in other liabilities is adjusted as an expense in provision for credit losses. The estimate includes consideration of the likelihood that
        funding will occur and an estimate of expected credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives.&#160; Estimating credit losses on unfunded commitments requires CTBI to consider the following categories of off-balance sheet
        credit exposure: unfunded commitments to extend credit, unfunded lines of credit, and standby letters of credit.&#160; Each of these unfunded commitments is then analyzed for a probability of funding to calculate a probable funding amount.&#160; The life of
        loan loss factor by related portfolio segment from the loan ACL calculation is then applied to the probable funding amount to calculate the estimated credit losses on off-balance sheet credit exposures recognized as other liabilities.</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552176" continuedAt="Text_61b89cfa9eca44bf9355530773552552177">

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#10146;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <span style="font-weight: bold;">FASB Issues Improvement to Income Statement Expense Disclosures &#8211;</span> In November 2024, the
        Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued ASU No. 2024-03, <span style="font-style: italic;">Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement
          Expenses</span> to improve the disclosures about a public business entity&#8217;s expenses and address investor requests for more detailed information about the types of expenses (including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation,
        amortization, and depletion) in commonly presented expense captions.&#160; ASU No. 2024-03 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2027.&#160; Early adoption is permitted.&#160; The
        amendments in this update should be applied either prospectively to financial statements issued for reporting periods after the effective date of this update, or retrospectively to any or all prior periods presented in the financial statements.&#160;
        CTBI does not expect ASU 2024-03 to have a material impact on CTBI&#8217;s financial statements.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#10146;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; <span style="font-weight: bold;">FASB Issues New Guidance on Purchased Loans</span> &#8211;&#160;In November 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-08
            <span style="font-style: italic;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326):&#160; Purchased Loans</span> in response to stakeholders&#8217; concerns about the accounting for acquired financial assets in accordance with ASC 326.&#160; The ASU amends
            the current expected credit loss (CECL) model in ASC 326-20 to: (1) expand the population of acquired financial assets subject to the &#8220;gross-up approach&#8221; for measuring credit losses to apply to &#8220;seasoned&#8221; purchased loans. This approach allows
            entities to avoid recording a day-one credit loss expense in profit or loss but also reduces interest income recognized in later periods and (2) introduce criteria for determining whether a purchased loan is considered &#8220;seasoned&#8221; and will be
            accounted for using the gross-up approach.&#160; The amendments will be effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, with early adoption allowed for financial statements that have not yet been issued or made available
            for issuance.&#160; This ASU has no impact on CTBI&#8217;s financial statements at this time.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">U.S. Treasury and Government Agencies</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f39" continuedAt="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f40">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f40" continuedAt="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f41">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The unrealized losses in U.S. Treasury and government agencies were caused by interest rate changes.&#160; CTBI expects to recover the amortized cost basis
      over the term of the securities.&#160; These securities are guaranteed by the U.S. government and are generally considered to be risk-free, which is why CTBI does not record an allowance for credit loss on these investments.&#160; Furthermore, CTBI does not
      intend to sell the investments and it is not more likely than not that we will be required to sell the investments before recovery of their amortized cost.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f41" continuedAt="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f42">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;"> <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">State and Political Subdivisions</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f43" continuedAt="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f44">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f44" continuedAt="Text_a70479d859ca456db6ecf49bb6f60c5f45">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">The unrealized losses in securities of state and political subdivisions were caused by interest rate changes.&#160; These securities benefit from stable dedicated tax
        revenues, a legal framework that prioritizes bondholder payments, and third-party bond insurance, which significantly mitigate credit risk.&#160; Due to these robust credit protection measures, CTBI does not record an allowance for credit loss on its
        state and political subdivisions securities.&#160; The contractual terms of those investments do not permit the issuer to settle the securities at a price less than par which will equal amortized cost at maturity.&#160; Furthermore, CTBI does not intend to
        sell the investments before recovery of their amortized cost and it is not more likely than not that we will be required to sell the investments before recovery of their amortized cost.</span> </div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Credit Quality Indicators and Profile<span style="text-decoration: underline;"><br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f60" continuedAt="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f61">

</ix:continuation>

</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f62" continuedAt="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f63">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f63" continuedAt="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f64">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI categorizes loans into risk categories based on relevant information about the ability of borrowers to service their debt such as: current
      financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors.&#160; CTBI also considers the fair value of the underlying collateral and the strength and willingness of the
      guarantor(s).&#160; CTBI analyzes commercial loans individually by classifying the loans as to credit risk.&#160; Loans classified as loss, doubtful, substandard, or special mention are reviewed quarterly by CTBI for further deterioration or improvement to
      determine if appropriately classified and valued if deemed impaired.&#160; All other commercial loan reviews are completed every <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:ReviewPeriodForLoans" id="Fact_39a7e84e11744b01a57463d9f212632d" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_InternalCreditAssessmentAxis_PassMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:ReviewPeriodForLoans" id="Fact_4c737d41cfd84a5c95379300e94209f9" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_InternalCreditAssessmentAxis_PassMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">18</ix:nonNumeric> months.&#160; In addition, during the renewal process of any loan, as well as if a loan becomes past due or if other information becomes available, CTBI
      will evaluate the loan grade.&#160; CTBI uses the following definitions for risk ratings:</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f64" continuedAt="Text_16e0eb00efb14b91ae78d5fe01027e3f65">

    </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

    <td style="width: 18pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
          </td>

    <td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&#10146;</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Pass</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> grades include
                investment grade, low risk, moderate risk, and acceptable risk loans.&#160; The loans range from loans that have no chance of resulting in a loss to loans that have a limited chance of resulting in a loss.&#160; Customers in this grade have excellent
                to fair credit ratings.&#160; The cash flows are adequate to meet required debt repayments.</span></div>
          </td>

            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Other assets especially mentioned (OAEM)</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> reflects loans that are currently protected but are potentially weak.&#160; These loans constitute an undue and unwarranted credit risk but not to the point of justifying a classification of substandard.&#160; The credit risk may be
                relatively minor yet constitute an unwarranted risk in light of circumstances surrounding a specific asset. Loans in this grade display potential weaknesses which may, if unchecked or uncorrected, inadequately protect CTBI&#8217;s credit position

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Doubtful</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> graded loans have
                the weaknesses inherent in the substandard grading with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, highly questionable and
                improbable.&#160; The probability of loss is extremely high, but because of certain important and reasonably specific pending factors which may work to CTBI&#8217;s advantage or strengthen the asset(s), its classification as an estimated loss is
                deferred until its more exact status may be determined.&#160; Pending factors include proposed merger, acquisition, or liquidation procedures, capital injection, perfecting liens on additional collateral, and refinancing plans.</span></div>
          </td>

  </tr>

<div style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; text-transform: none;">Based on the quarterly evaluation of losses for
        these credits, the combined amount of expected loss is $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossExpectedLoss" id="Fact_022ef748613f4c57b0b57cb08146c7bc" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.7</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160; This expected loss is tied to <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FinancingReceivablesNumberOfLoansLiquidationOfCollateralized" id="Fact_31abbcbe4f23479fbe7e1ac478f06d28" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="U007" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> unrelated loans that demonstrate a shortfall in collateral which is insufficient to repay the principal balance of the loans in the event of a
        liquidation of the collateral and after estimated selling costs.&#160; All other evaluated credits show sufficient collateral to repay the entire loan balances after estimated selling costs.&#160; The hotel/motel, commercial real estate residential, and
        commercial real estate nonresidential segments are all collateralized with real estate. <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FinancingReceivablesNumberOfLoansCollateralized" id="Fact_86a1787dee9845fa800d100cb00e56f8" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_CollateralAxis_AccountsReceivableEquipmentAndInventoryMember_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis_CommercialOtherMember" unitRef="U007" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">Four</ix:nonFraction> loans listed in the commercial other

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Loans
















        retain their accrual status at the time of their modification.&#160; As a result, if a loan is on nonaccrual at the time it is modified, it stays as nonaccrual, and if a loan is on accrual at the time of the modification, it generally stays on accrual.&#160;
        Commercial and consumer loans modified due to a borrower&#8217;s financial difficulty are closely monitored for delinquency as an early indicator of possible future default.&#160; If a loan to a borrower experiencing financial difficulty subsequently
        defaults, CTBI evaluates the loan for possible further impairment.&#160; <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:ScheduleOfFinancingReceivablesPaymentStatusOfModifiedLoansToBorrowersExperiencingFinancialDifficultyTableTextBlock" id="Text_ff8daa6fdd6c4fa5a5724b9f43015b3b" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_b3edc9c6c1e84eca9243950ef0c598df1"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal;">The table below represents the payment status of loans to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty for the past 12 months as of December 31, 2025.</span></ix:nonNumeric></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">5.&#160; Concentrations of Credit Risk</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a1" continuedAt="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a2">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a2" continuedAt="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a3">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a3" continuedAt="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a4">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_d4bef33f64c24aa7a0e0eb971936861a4">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI&#8217;s banking activities include granting commercial, residential, and consumer loans to customers primarily located in eastern, northeastern,
      central, and south central Kentucky, southern West Virginia, and northeastern Tennessee. CTBI is continuing to manage all components of its portfolio mix in a manner to reduce risk from changes in economic conditions. Concentrations of credit, as
      defined for regulatory purposes, are reviewed quarterly by management to ensure that internally established limits based on Tier 1 Capital plus the ACL are not exceeded.&#160; At December 31, 2025 and 2024, our concentrations of hospitality industry
      credits were <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_83816ce08b2a4bed9dc7d1196bc104f5" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_HospitalityIndustryCreditsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">65</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_84698a91ca7c475393e2eefb26d372b5" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_HospitalityIndustryCreditsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">64</ix:nonFraction>%
      of Tier 1 capital plus the ACL, respectively.&#160; Lessors of residential buildings and dwellings credits were <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_12685311ef5c4580986cffa46e538a9b" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_LessorsOfResidentialBuildingsAndDwellingsCreditsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">53</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_42ebbf37243640dea9862d5ec985528b" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_LessorsOfResidentialBuildingsAndDwellingsCreditsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">51</ix:nonFraction>% for each period end, respectively, and lessors of non-residential buildings credits were <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_46c50340ad8f4e14b796ddd4035f6f35" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_LessorsOfNonResidentialBuildingsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">33</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" id="Fact_bbc4241572334db5b7ddbaaf1942122b" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_Tier1CapitalPlusAllowanceForLoanAndLeaseLossesMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_CreditConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis_LessorsOfNonResidentialBuildingsMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">32</ix:nonFraction>% for each period end, respectively.&#160; These percentages are within our
      internally established limits regarding concentrations of credit.</div>

<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">7.&#160; Leases</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_cbbd80460a9f4050ae6bf6276be909a31" continuedAt="Text_cbbd80460a9f4050ae6bf6276be909a32">
<div style="margin-left: 9pt;"><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
        <ix:continuation id="Text_cbbd80460a9f4050ae6bf6276be909a32" continuedAt="Text_cbbd80460a9f4050ae6bf6276be909a33">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">CTBI has <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:NumberOfFinanceLeases" id="Fact_7b82872b4b9c4d3eb201b9225bb8645e" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U008" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> finance leases for property but no material sublease or leasing arrangements for which it is
            the lessor of property or equipment.&#160; CTBI has operating leases for banking and ATM locations.&#160; These leases have original remaining lease terms of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="Fact_eb5c9f64d56841b0a7ab3159c15e0164" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric>
            year to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="Fact_a86faadf70934f4fa044350c2ba5eeb4" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">45</ix:nonNumeric> years, some of which include options to renew the leases for up to <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="Fact_23fb9d94458244f0b20faa0c31602b6e" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>.&#160; These options, some of which include variable costs related to rent escalations based on recent financial indices such as the Consumer Price Index which CTBI
            uses to estimate future rent increases, are included in the calculation of the lease liability and right-of-use asset when management determines it is reasonably certain the option will be exercised.&#160; CTBI determines this on each lease by
            considering all relevant contract-based, asset-based, market-based, and entity-based economic factors.&#160; Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized at lease commencement based on the present value of the remaining lease payments
            using a discount rate that represents our incremental borrowing rate, on a collateralized basis, over a similar term, at the lease commencement date.&#160; Right-of-use assets are further adjusted for prepaid rent, lease incentives, and initial
            direct costs, if any. </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We utilize securities sold under agreements to repurchase to facilitate the needs of our customers and provide additional funding to our balance
      sheet.&#160; Repurchase agreements are transactions whereby we offer to sell to a counterparty an undivided interest in an eligible security at an agreed upon purchase price, and which obligates CTBI to repurchase the security on an agreed upon date at an
      agreed upon repurchase price plus interest at an agreed upon rate.&#160; Securities sold under agreements to repurchase are recorded at the amount of cash received in connection with the transaction and are reflected in the accompanying consolidated
      balance <span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">shee<span style="font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">ts. At December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had amounts at risk under repurchase agreements for <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:NumberOfCustomers" id="Fact_efd29a8349274fc5842fac1f18f52d2d" contextRef="c20241231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U009" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:NumberOfCustomers" id="Fact_96a907877da846f9823b6f2b589c93b6" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U009" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> customer exceeding <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:PercentageOfShareholderEquity" id="Fact_86e2630f213f4371bf8fd34e33385973" contextRef="c20241231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal"><ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:PercentageOfShareholderEquity" id="Fact_03b7b777f87646378f15a6a8803a36f9" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">10</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% of
          shareholders&#8217; equity with balances of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAgreementCounterpartyAmountAtRisk" id="Fact_b7ce8ab502624eb7bfcbcf2c5be7d302" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">148.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAgreementCounterpartyAmountAtRisk" id="Fact_07c30ec52e4e4e75a6a894a3d35637cf" contextRef="c20241231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">98.0</ix:nonFraction> million and weighted average maturities of <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAgreementCounterpartyWeightedAverageMaturityOfAgreements1" id="Fact_421563503ea749d98e7b9e20b411519a" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4.6</ix:nonNumeric> months and

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We monitor collateral levels on a continuous basis and maintain records of each transaction specifically describing the applicable security and the
      counterparty&#8217;s fractional interest in that security, and we segregate the security from its general assets in accordance with regulations governing custodial holdings of securities.&#160; The primary risk with our repurchase agreements is market risk
      associated with the securities securing the transactions, as we may be required to provide additional collateral based on fair value changes of the underlying securities.&#160; Securities pledged as collateral under repurchase agreements are maintained
      with our safekeeping agents.&#160; The carrying value of investment securities available-for-sale pledged as collateral under repurchase agreements totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecurities" id="Fact_c4471a3113b94ce8b22317b6ef46b1ff" contextRef="c20251231_PledgedStatusAxis_AssetPledgedAsCollateralMember_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_SecuritiesSoldUnderAgreementsToRepurchaseMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">358.1</ix:nonFraction>

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Repurchase agreements are subject to underlying agreements with master netting or similar arrangements, which provide for the right of setoff in the
        event of default or in the event of bankruptcy of either party to the transactions. Repurchase agreements are reported to these arrangements on a gross basis.&#160; <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:OffsettingLiabilitiesTableTextBlock" id="Text_7a323438eaf24f55880ea1bec718f9db" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_982cf39463b54d36bca5d344e01f58111"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The following

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December 31, 2025, our FHLB
      advances were collateralized by FHLB stock of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresCollateralPledged1" id="Fact_ba94b87446f449c48231a91bc6626d3b" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">5.2</ix:nonFraction> million and a blanket lien on qualifying 1-4 family first mortgage loans. We had a $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresMaximumAmountAvailable" id="Fact_301a4beaadbd48c981966c32c65c79bb" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">688.5</ix:nonFraction> million FHLB borrowing capacity with $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AdvancesFromFederalHomeLoanBanks" id="Fact_40f7b34e42b4456593541b49ccdd3ef1" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.3</ix:nonFraction>
      million in advances and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LineOfCredit" id="Fact_2740619af6a8475a83a0fba15158f857" contextRef="c20251231_CreditFacilityAxis_LetterOfCreditMember_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">141.3</ix:nonFraction> million in letters of credit used for public fund pledging, leaving $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresAmountOfAvailableUnusedFunds" id="Fact_cafaa9a71d9a4eddb7a2580558acc73f" contextRef="c20251231_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">546.9</ix:nonFraction> million available for additional advances as of year-end. The advances had fixed interest rates of <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesBranchOfFHLBBankInterestRate" id="Fact_b4c57d5fa44f4244a1dcbd2aa4019de1" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.00</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesBranchOfFHLBBankInterestRate" id="Fact_c4c474c74b724dcb8e2b0df8dc345a9d" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">2.00</ix:nonFraction>% with a weighted average rate of <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesBranchOfFHLBBankInterestRate" id="Fact_45a77ddd79a249aeb5621411b8dce34d" contextRef="c20251231_RangeAxis_WeightedAverageMember_ShortTermDebtTypeAxis_FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.04</ix:nonFraction>%.&#160; The advances are subject to restrictions or penalties in the event of prepayment.</div>

    <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
      <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="Text_3fe6fe7fad414e059234e61b94ee1018" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">12.&#160; Fair Value of Financial Assets and Liabilities</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b1" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b2">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b2" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b3">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Fair Value Measurements</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b3" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b4">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b4" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b5">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received upon sale of an asset or the price paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction
        between market participants at the measurement date (i.e., the &#8220;exit price&#8221;).&#160; CTBI uses a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs used in valuation techniques to measure fair value into three broad levels.&#160; The following is a brief
        description of each level:</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b5" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b6">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b6" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b7">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b7" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b8">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b8" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b9">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 1 Inputs &#8211; Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b9" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b10">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b10" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b11">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b11" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b12">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b12" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b13">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 2 Inputs &#8211; Inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. These might include
        quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, such as interest rates and yield curves that are observable at commonly quoted intervals.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b13" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b14">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b14" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b15">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b15" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b16">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b16" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b17">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 3 Inputs &#8211; Unobservable inputs for determining the fair values of assets or liabilities that reflect an entity&#8217;s own assumptions about the assumptions that
        market participants would use in determining an exit price for the assets or liabilities.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b17" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b18">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b18" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b19">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b19" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b20">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b20" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b21">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A financial instrument&#8217;s categorization within the above valuation hierarchy is based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair
        value measurement.&#160; CTBI&#8217;s assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment, and CTBI considers factors specific to the assets or liabilities.&#160; The following is a description of
        the valuation methodologies used for CTBI&#8217;s assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b21" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b22">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b22" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b23">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b23" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b24">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Recurring Measurements</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b24" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b25">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b25" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b26"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueAssetsMeasuredOnRecurringBasisTextBlock" id="Text_82954e0ac3dc4412aa236d9bda98e660" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_50ef3734d48247d98c0f777bbafe3a041">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The following tables present the fair value measurements of assets recognized in the accompanying balance sheets measured at fair value on a
        recurring basis as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 and indicate the level within the fair value hierarchy of the valuation techniques.</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b26" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b27"><ix:continuation id="Text_50ef3734d48247d98c0f777bbafe3a041" continuedAt="Text_50ef3734d48247d98c0f777bbafe3a042">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b27" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b28"><ix:continuation id="Text_50ef3734d48247d98c0f777bbafe3a042" continuedAt="Text_50ef3734d48247d98c0f777bbafe3a043">
<div><br/>

        the valuation techniques during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.&#160; For assets classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy, the process used to develop the reported fair value is described below.</div>
