        <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" border="0" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-spacing: 0;">

    <td style="width: 98%; vertical-align: top; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Available-for-Sale Securities</td>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b41" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b42">

</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b42" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b43">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">U.S. Treasury and government agencies are classified as Level 1 of the valuation hierarchy where quoted market prices are available in the active
        market on which the individual securities are traded.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b43" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b44">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b44" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b45">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">If quoted market prices are not available, the fair value measurements consider observable data that may include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash
        flows, the U.S. Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information, and the bond&#8217;s terms and conditions, among other factors.&#160; U.S. Treasury and government agencies, state and
        political subdivisions, agency mortgage-backed securities, and asset-backed securities are classified as Level 2 inputs.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b45" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b46">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b46" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b47">

        <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" border="0" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-spacing: 0;">

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b48" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b49">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-weight: normal; text-indent: 36pt;">Fair value for equity securities is derived based on unobservable inputs, such as the discount rate,
        quarterly dividends payable to the Visa Class B common stock, and the prevailing conversion rate at the conversion date.&#160; The most recent conversion rate of <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiMeasurementInput" id="Fact_33763208e6e545dcaa76abbd595cfae4" contextRef="c20251231_MeasurementInputTypeAxis_MeasurementInputConversionPriceMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.5491</ix:nonFraction> and the most recent dividend rate of <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiMeasurementInput" id="Fact_73c7948417254a9ba182988aee2ad2d5" contextRef="c20251231_MeasurementInputTypeAxis_MeasurementInputExpectedDividendRateMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="4" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.0379</ix:nonFraction> were used to derive the
        fair value estimate.&#160; Significant increases (decreases) in either of those inputs in isolation would result in a significantly lower (higher) fair value measurement.&#160; Generally, a change in the assumption used for discount rate is accompanied by a
        directionally opposite change in the fair value estimate.&#160; The weighted averages presented in the tables below are determined by taking the median of the estimates in conversion dates and discount rate. </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-weight: normal; text-align: justify;">
        <div><ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b49" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b50">

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b52" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b53">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In determining fair value, CTBI utilizes assumptions about factors such as mortgage interest rates, discount rates, mortgage loan prepayment speeds,
        market trends, and industry demand.&#160; Due to the nature of the valuation inputs, MSRs are classified within Level 3 of the hierarchy.&#160; We have determined these assumptions, processes, and conclusions to be reasonable and appropriate in determining
        the fair value of this asset.&#160; See the table below for inputs and valuation techniques used for Level 3 MSRs.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b53" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b54">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b54" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b55">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b55" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b56">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b56" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b57">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value for MSRs is derived based on unobservable inputs, such as prepayment speeds of the underlying loans generated using the Andrew Davidson
        Prepayment Model, FHLMC/FNMA guidelines, the weighted average life of the loan, the discount rate, the weighted average coupon, and the weighted average default rate.&#160; Significant increases (decreases) in either of those inputs in isolation would
        result in a significantly lower (higher) fair value measurement.&#160; Generally, a change in the assumption used for prepayment speeds is accompanied by a directionally opposite change in the assumption for interest rates.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b57" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b58">

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The estimated fair value of collateral-dependent loans is based on the appraised fair value of the collateral, less estimated cost to sell.&#160;
        Collateral-dependent loans are classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b81" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b82">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b82" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b83">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b83" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b84">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b84" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b85">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI considers the appraisal or evaluation as the starting point for determining fair value and then considers other factors and events in the
        environment that may affect the fair value.&#160; Appraisals of the collateral underlying collateral-dependent loans are obtained when the loan is determined to be collateral-dependent and subsequently as deemed necessary by the Chief Credit Officer.&#160;
        The appraised values are reduced by discounts to consider lack of marketability and estimated cost to sell if repayment or satisfaction of the loan is dependent on the sale of the collateral.&#160; These discounts and estimates are developed by the
        Chief Credit Officer by comparison to historical results.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b85" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b86">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b86" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b87">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b87" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b88">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b88" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b89">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans considered collateral-dependent are loans for which the repayment is expected to be provided substantially through the operation or sale of
        the collateral when the borrower is experiencing financial difficulty.&#160; There was one fair value adjustment to collateral-dependent loans during the year ended December 31, 2025 totaling $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FairValueAdjustmentOnCollateralDependentLoans" id="Fact_1a2a52b7f3b6463eb8530c7e6dc9aa30" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160; Fair value adjustments for the year ended December 31, 2024 were $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FairValueAdjustmentOnCollateralDependentLoans" id="Fact_f37909afe4654cffba0d6e1b49d3c895" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.1</ix:nonFraction>
        million.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b89" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b90">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b90" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b91">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span><br/></div>
</ix:continuation>
        <div style="clear: both; margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 10pt;" class="BRPFPageBreakArea">

          <div style="page-break-after: always;" class="BRPFPageBreak">

      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b91" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b92">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Other Real Estate Owned</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b92" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b93">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b93" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b94">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Estimated fair value of OREO is based on appraisals or evaluations.&#160; OREO is classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy.&#160; Long-lived
        assets are subject to nonrecurring fair value adjustments to reflect subsequent partial write-downs that are based on the observable market price or current appraised value of the collateral.&#160; Fair value adjustments to OREO disclosed above for the
        years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 were $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FairValueAdjustmentOnOtherRealEstateOwned" id="Fact_e726b7cdd6644d6ca417d9cb9f05dc02" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">38</ix:nonFraction> thousand and $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:FairValueAdjustmentOnOtherRealEstateOwned" id="Fact_c096f5611bcc4c589f520bb7614d23f7" contextRef="c20240101to20241231_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">63</ix:nonFraction> thousand, respectively. </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b94" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b95">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b95" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b96">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b96" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b97">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b97" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b98">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our policy for determining the frequency of periodic reviews is based upon consideration of the specific properties and the known or perceived
        market fluctuations in a particular market and is typically between <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedTypicalFrequencyOfPeriodReviews" id="Fact_6f81e884079548daa5a6fc06399a9c2e" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> and <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedTypicalFrequencyOfPeriodReviews" id="Fact_4884e024a91c4374b904d81c68e6c261" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">18</ix:nonNumeric> months but generally not more than <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:OtherRealEstateOwnedFrequencyOfPeriodicReviews" id="Fact_2a316eedce5045a2882de91ab335e2eb" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">24</ix:nonNumeric> months.&#160; Appraisers are selected from
        the list of approved appraisers maintained by management.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b98" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b99">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
      <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b99" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b100">

        <ix:continuation id="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b100" continuedAt="Text_3cb8d1cecc5e4a3bb6d62920f20f9e6b101">

<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';">Unobservable inputs for mortgage servicing rights were weighted by loan amount.&#160; Unobservable inputs
            for equity securities were weighted by security value.&#160; Unobservable inputs for OREO were weighted by estimated cost to sell.&#160; There were no transfers in or out of Level 3 during 2025 or 2024.&#160; </span><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueAssetsAndLiabilitiesMeasuredOnRecurringAndNonrecurringBasisValuationTechniquesTableTextBlock" id="Text_b337ae9be1f14f37b0d8f96bc11b1a1f" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_bf4d1656f4734c109546dbd7d2d7bba51"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';">The following tables present quantitative information about unobservable inputs used in recurring and nonrecurring
            Level 3 fair value measurements at December 31, 2025 and 2024.</span></span></ix:nonNumeric></div>

      prevailing at the same time for comparable transactions with other persons.</div>

      financial instruments include standby letters of credit and commitments to extend credit in the form of unused lines of credit.&#160; CTBI uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for on-balance sheet
      instruments.</div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b16" continuedAt="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b17">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Standby letters of credit represent conditional commitments to guarantee the performance of a third party.&#160; The credit risk involved is essentially
      the same as the risk involved in making loans.&#160; At December 31, 2025, we maintained a credit loss reserve recorded in other liabilities
      of approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LiabilityForClaimsAndClaimsAdjustmentExpense" id="Fact_5900fc1d47f045d595dd8f133a6bccab" contextRef="c20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_StandbyLettersOfCreditMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million relating to these financial standby letters of credit.&#160; The reserve coverage calculation was determined using
      essentially the same methodology as used for the ACL.&#160; Approximately <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:PercentageOfSecuredStandbyLettersOfCredit" id="Fact_a7379042b6c444f7b52066ae4fb7b27e" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_StandbyLettersOfCreditMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">70</ix:nonFraction>% of the total standby letters of credit are secured, with $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:StandbyLettersOfCreditSecuredByCash" id="Fact_8240449c8b7641d98fc8707140867cdd" contextRef="c20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_StandbyLettersOfCreditMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">26.4</ix:nonFraction> million of the total $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:StandbyLettersOfCreditsSecured" id="Fact_20edeb1dae5c4cf789c3530a404e2645" contextRef="c20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_StandbyLettersOfCreditMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">37.5</ix:nonFraction> million
      secured by cash.&#160; Collateral for the remaining secured standby letters of credit varies but is comprised primarily of accounts receivable, inventory, property, equipment, and income-producing properties.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b17" continuedAt="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b18">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b18" continuedAt="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b19">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
        </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b19" continuedAt="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b20">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_0d535fae9c1147c0ba4135f98f0c934b20">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to originate loans to customers as long as there is no violation of any condition of the contract.&#160; At
      December 31, 2025, a credit loss reserve recorded in other liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LiabilityForClaimsAndClaimsAdjustmentExpense" id="Fact_fdc107896dd74cdaacadd8034791db71" contextRef="c20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million was maintained relating to these commitments.&#160; Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee.&#160; Since a portion of
      the commitments may expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent future cash requirements.&#160; Each customer&#8217;s creditworthiness is evaluated on a case-by-case basis.&#160; The amount of collateral obtained, if
      deemed necessary, is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of the counterparty.&#160; Collateral held varies, but may include accounts receivable, inventory, property, plant and equipment, commercial real estate, and residential real estate.&#160; A portion
      of the commitments is to extend credit at fixed rates.&#160; Fixed rate loan commitments at December 31, 2025 of $<ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:CommitmentToExtendCreditWithFixedInterestRate" id="Fact_721001b051a749719150f7f0f1dacbcc" contextRef="c20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">87.7</ix:nonFraction> million had interest rates ranging predominantly from <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:InterestRateOnLoanCommitments" id="Fact_f40fce287acd4acd903bd2c8c88777b1" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember_RangeAxis_MinimumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">4.0</ix:nonFraction>%
      to <ix:nonFraction name="ctbi:InterestRateOnLoanCommitments" id="Fact_dea4dae64c234b91a5588e8a7d1a5fd3" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" unitRef="U005" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">8.3</ix:nonFraction>% and terms of predominantly <ix:nonNumeric name="ctbi:FixedRateLoanCommitmentsTerm" id="Fact_075306adc3f5458582efa0501c7942fc" contextRef="c20250101to20251231_FinancialInstrumentAxis_CommitmentsToExtendCreditMember_RangeAxis_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">2 years</ix:nonNumeric>
      or less.&#160; These credit commitments were based on prevailing rates, terms, and conditions applicable to other loans being made.</div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock" id="Text_368d4ad245d64df186c084649a6596c6" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">15.&#160; Revenue Recognition</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce1" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce2">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce2" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce3">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI&#8217;s primary source of revenue is interest income generated from loans and investment securities. Interest income is recognized according to the
      terms of the financial instrument agreement over the life of the loan or investment security unless it is determined that the counterparty is unable to continue making interest payments.&#160; Interest income also includes prepaid interest fees from
      commercial customers, which approximates the interest foregone on the balance of the loan prepaid.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce3" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce4">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce4" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce5">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI&#8217;s additional source of income, also referred to as noninterest income, includes service charges on deposit accounts, gains on sales of loans,
      trust and wealth management income, loan related fees, brokerage revenue, and other miscellaneous income and is largely based on contracts with customers.&#160; In these cases, CTBI recognizes revenue when it satisfies a performance obligation by
      transferring control over a product or service to a customer. CTBI considers a customer to be any party to which we will provide goods or services that are an output of CTBI&#8217;s ordinary activities in exchange for consideration.&#160; There is little
      seasonality with regards to revenue from contracts with customers and all inter-company revenue is eliminated when CTBI&#8217;s financial statements are consolidated.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce5" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce6">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce6" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce7">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Generally, CTBI enters into contracts with customers that are short-term in nature where the performance obligations are fulfilled and payment is
      processed at the same time.&#160; Such examples include revenue related to merchant fees, interchange fees, and investment services income.&#160; In addition, revenue generated from existing customer relationships such as deposit accounts are also considered
      short-term in nature, because the relationship may be terminated at any time and payment is processed at the time performance obligations are fulfilled.&#160; As a result, CTBI does <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" id="Fact_d36c2b0237ea46d4b80afad441c32572" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerAssetNet" id="Fact_9fbf9afd082a41958e2bf470e5742655" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerReceivableAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" id="Fact_8c9f4bffa39e44e19766085fbcaca7ce" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U001" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>t have contract assets, contract liabilities, or related receivable accounts for contracts with customers.&#160;&#160; In cases where collectability is a concern, CTBI does not
      record revenue.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce7" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce8">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce8" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce9">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Generally, the pricing of transactions between CTBI and each customer is either (i) established within a legally enforceable contract between the two
      parties, as is the case with loan sales, or (ii) disclosed to the customer at a specific point in time, as is the case when a deposit account is opened or before a new loan is underwritten.&#160; Fees are usually fixed at a specific amount or as a
      percentage of a transaction amount.&#160; No judgment or estimates by management are required to record revenue related to these transactions and pricing is clearly identified within these contracts.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce9" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce10">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce10" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce11">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI primarily operates in Kentucky and contiguous areas. Therefore, all significant operating decisions are based upon analysis of CTBI as <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" id="Fact_962714ca6b84469289757f9bf43a6e82" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U006" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> operating segment.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce11" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce12">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce12" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce13">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We disaggregate our revenue from contracts with customers by contract-type and timing of revenue recognition, as we believe it best depicts how the
      nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of our revenue and cash flows are affected by economic factors.&#160; Noninterest income not generated from customers during CTBI&#8217;s ordinary activities primarily relates to MSRs, gains/losses on the sale of
      investment securities, gains/losses on the sale of OREO, gains/losses on the sale of property, plant and equipment, and income from bank owned life insurance.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce13" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce14">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce14" continuedAt="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce15">
<div><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_ddb079ead5024996b79a94b65cd5a6ce15">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">All revenue streams in the scope of the revenue recognition accounting standard are recognized at a point in
          time.</span> </span>For more information related to our components of noninterest income, see the consolidated statements of income and comprehensive income.</div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_dced5ff11f4d4f74922746c1ae25ed0e42" continuedAt="Text_dced5ff11f4d4f74922746c1ae25ed0e43">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Current income tax expense reflects taxes to be paid or refunded
      for the current period by applying the provisions of the enacted tax law to the taxable income or excess of deductions over revenues.&#160; CTBI determines deferred income taxes using the asset and liability (or balance sheet) method.&#160; Under this method,
      the net deferred tax asset or liability is based on the tax effects of the differences between the book and tax bases of assets and liabilities, and enacted changes in tax rates and laws are recognized in the period in which they occur.&#160; Deferred
      income tax expense results from changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities between periods.&#160; Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance if, based on the weight of evidence available, it is more likely than not that some portion or
      all of a deferred tax asset will not be realized.</div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Uncertain



























        tax positions are recognized if it is more likely than not, based on the technical merits, that the tax position will be realized or sustained upon examination.&#160; The term more likely than not means a likelihood of more than 50 percent; the terms
        examined and upon examination also include resolution of the related appeals or litigation processes, if any.&#160; A tax position that meets the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold is initially and subsequently measured as the largest amount of
        tax benefit that has a greater than 50 percent likelihood of being realized upon settlement with a taxing authority that has full knowledge of all relevant information.&#160; The determination of whether or not a tax position has met the
        more-likely-than-not recognition threshold considers the facts, circumstances, and information available at the reporting date and is subject to management&#8217;s judgment.&#160; CTBI has no uncertain tax positions.<br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="Text_0d0f2e8460be47f0860dc224264d1d2d" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_16ab26db17bb487583ff83c83dd378581">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">20.&#160; <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';">Commitments and Contingencies</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16ab26db17bb487583ff83c83dd378581" continuedAt="Text_16ab26db17bb487583ff83c83dd378582">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_16ab26db17bb487583ff83c83dd378582">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI and our subsidiaries, and from time to time, our officers, are named defendants in legal actions arising from ordinary business activities.&#160;
      Management, after consultation with legal counsel, believes any pending actions at December 31, 2025 are without merit or that the ultimate liability, if any, will not materially affect our consolidated financial position or results of operations.</div>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" id="Text_87b89519f1e84134afe72c0c52fc6712" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">21.&#160; Regulatory Matters</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd1" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd2">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd2" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd3">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI&#8217;s principal source of funds is dividends received from our banking subsidiary, CTB.&#160; Regulations limit the amount of dividends that may be paid
      by CTB without prior approval.&#160; During 2026, approximately $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StatutoryAccountingPracticesStatutoryAmountAvailableForDividendPaymentsWithoutRegulatoryApproval" id="Fact_e1b2e2fd0f6645c9b11c695d887b4e03" contextRef="c20251231_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_SubsidiariesMember" unitRef="U001" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">113.6</ix:nonFraction> million plus any 2026 net profits can be paid by CTB without prior
      regulatory approval.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd3" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd4">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd4" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd5">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI and CTB are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies.&#160; Failure to meet minimum capital
      requirements can initiate certain mandatory, and possibly additional discretionary, actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a material adverse effect on CTBI&#8217;s financial statements.&#160; Under regulatory capital adequacy guidelines, CTBI
      and CTB must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of CTBI&#8217;s and CTB&#8217;s assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices.&#160; Additionally, CTB must meet specific
      capital guidelines to be considered well capitalized per the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. CTBI&#8217;s and CTB&#8217;s capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators about components, risk
      weightings, and other factors.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd5" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd6">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd6" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd7">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI and CTB must maintain certain minimum capital ratios as set forth in the table below for capital adequacy purposes.&#160; On October 29, 2019, federal
      banking regulators adopted a final rule to simplify the regulatory capital requirements for eligible community banks and holding companies that opt-in to the community bank leverage ratio framework (the &#8220;CBLR framework&#8221;), as required by Section 201
      of the Economic Growth, Relief and Consumer Protection Act of 2018.&#160; Under the final rule, which became effective as of January 1, 2020, community banks and holding companies (which includes CTB and CTBI) that satisfy certain qualifying criteria,
      including having less than $10 billion in average total consolidated assets and a leverage ratio (referred to as the &#8220;community bank leverage ratio&#8221;) of greater than 9%, were eligible to opt-in to the CBLR framework.&#160; The community bank leverage
      ratio is the ratio of a banking organization&#8217;s Tier 1 capital to its average total consolidated assets, both as reported on the banking organization&#8217;s applicable regulatory filings. <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">Accordingly, a qualifying community banking organization that has a community bank leverage ratio
        greater than 9% will be considered to have met: (i) the risk-based and leverage capital requirements of the generally applicable capital rules; (ii) the capital ratio requirements in order to be considered well-capitalized under the prompt
        corrective action framework; and (iii) any other applicable capital or leverage requirements. Management elected to use the CBLR framework for CTBI and CTB. </span>CTBI&#8217;s and CTB&#8217;s CBLR ratios as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 are disclosed below.<br class="Apple-interchange-newline"/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd7" continuedAt="Text_c67dc9f233b8495d971ce6d81d14e4bd8">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">23.&#160; Segment Reporting</div>
</ix:nonNumeric>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_6484a8a66c814f9d9a38a1ba64d48bd51" continuedAt="Text_6484a8a66c814f9d9a38a1ba64d48bd52">

      <ix:continuation id="Text_6484a8a66c814f9d9a38a1ba64d48bd52" continuedAt="Text_6484a8a66c814f9d9a38a1ba64d48bd53">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">CTBI is a financial holding company, whose principal activity is the ownership and management of its wholly-owned subsidiaries, including CTB and
        Community Trust and Investment Company.&#160; As a community-oriented financial institution, the majority of CTBI&#8217;s operations consist of commercial and personal banking services.&#160; Management analyzed the operation of CTBI and determined it has <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" id="Fact_5fdbc0fcfdf44423abc726574e1ff54f" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U006" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" id="Fact_a28c63922af7496ba614c9c235be305c" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" unitRef="U006" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> reportable segment, community banking services.&#160; CTBI, through our operating subsidiaries, offers a wide range of consumer and commercial
        community banking services.&#160; Our chief operating decision maker is CTBI&#8217;s chief executive officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;).&#160; The CEO uses net income to allocate resources in the annual budget and forecasting process and considers budget-to-actual variances on a
        monthly basis for profit measures when making decisions about allocating capital and personnel to the reportable segment.&#160; The CEO uses net interest income and noninterest income to allocate resources (including employees, financial, or capital
        resources) to that segment in the annual budget and forecasting process and uses that measure as a basis for evaluating product offerings and pricing.&#160; The following tables present information about reported segment revenue, measures of a segment&#8217;s
        profit or loss, and significant segment expenses for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, and measure of a segment&#8217;s assets as of December 31, 2025 and 2024.&#160; CTBI does not allocate all holding company expenses, income taxes, or
        unusual items to the reportable segment.&#160; Accounting policies for the segment are the same as described in note 1 above.&#160; All operations of CTBI are domestic.&#160; <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock" id="Text_8e8061f29eef4b0d8f7691a450208437" contextRef="c20250101to20251231" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_3141042f466a4428af180d1cc35c43f01"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The following tables present the
        reconciliations of reportable segment revenues and measures of profit or loss and line item reconciliation to CTBI&#8217;s consolidated financial statement totals for the periods indicated.</span></ix:nonNumeric></div>

          Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</div>

Those
          standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>

          period audit of the consolidated financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the consolidated financial statements and (2)
          involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The communication of the critical audit matter does not alter in any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">As described in Note 1 to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, the
          Company estimates an allowance for credit losses (&#8220;ACL&#8221;) on loans on a collective (pool) basis using the discounted cash flow method when the loans share similar risk characteristics. Loans that do not share risk characteristics are evaluated on
          an individual basis. The Company&#8217;s methodology for estimating the ACL also includes consideration for qualitative loss factors.&#160; Each qualitative loss factor is given a risk weighting that is applied to determine the relevant adjustment to the
          ACL. Management uses significant judgment in determining the appropriate qualitative loss factors to be considered and the extent of their impact on the ACL estimate. As described in Note 4 to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, the
          Company&#8217;s ACL on loans was $60.2 million as of December 31, 2025.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>

          used to estimate the ACL as a critical audit matter: (i) economic conditions, (ii) delinquency trends within the commercial real estate nonresidential and consumer indirect loan segments, and (iii) changes in the value of underlying collateral
          within the commercial real estate nonresidential and consumer indirect loan segments. Auditing these estimates involved especially subjective and complex auditor judgment.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">We conducted our audit of internal control over financial reporting in accordance
          with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit
          included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed
          risk. Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify; font-weight: bold;">Definition and Limitations of Internal Control over Financial Reporting</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to
          provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#8217;s internal control over
          financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide
          reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in
          accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a
          material effect on the financial statements.</div>

        <div><br/></div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may
          not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the
          policies or procedures may deteriorate.</div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: left; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;"><br/>

                <div style="text-align: justify; font-weight: bold;">EVALUATION OF DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">CTBI&#8217;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining effective disclosure controls and procedures, as defined under Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Securities Exchange
                  Act of 1934.&#160; As of December 31, 2025, an evaluation was carried out by CTBI&#8217;s management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our
                  disclosure controls and procedures.&#160; Based on this evaluation, management concluded that disclosure controls and procedures as of December 31, 2025 were effective in ensuring material information required to be disclosed in this annual
                  report on Form 10-K was recorded, processed, summarized, and reported on a timely basis.</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; font-weight: bold;">CHANGES IN INTERNAL CONTROL OVER FINANCIAL REPORTING</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Management has evaluated the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 based on the control criteria in the 2013 COSO Framework issued by the
                  Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (&#8220;COSO&#8221;) of the Treadway Commission.&#160; Based on such evaluation, we have concluded that CTBI&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is effective as of December 31, 2025.</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">There were no changes in CTBI&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the year ended December 31, 2025 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to
                  materially affect, CTBI&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</div>

                <div style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold;">MANAGEMENT REPORT ON INTERNAL CONTROL</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">We, as management of Community Trust Bancorp, Inc. and its subsidiaries (&#8220;CTBI&#8221;), are responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting.&#160;
                  Pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission, internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company&#8217;s principal executive and principal financial
                  officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company&#8217;s board of directors, management and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of
                  financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and includes those policies and procedures that:</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" class="DSPFListTable" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-align: left; color: #000000; border-spacing: 0;">


  <tr>

    <td style="width: 13.5pt; vertical-align: top;">&#8226;</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
                        <div>Pertain to the maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company;</div>
                      </td>

  </tr>


</table>
                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" class="DSPFListTable" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-align: left; color: #000000; border-spacing: 0;">


  <tr>

    <td style="width: 13.5pt; vertical-align: top;">&#8226;</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
                        <div>Provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the
                          company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and</div>
                      </td>

  </tr>


</table>
                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" class="DSPFListTable" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-align: left; color: #000000; border-spacing: 0;">


  <tr>

    <td style="width: 13.5pt; vertical-align: top;">&#8226;</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
                        <div>Provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</div>
                      </td>

  </tr>


</table>
                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention of overriding controls.&#160; Accordingly,
                  even effective internal control can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation.&#160; Further, because of changes in conditions, the effectiveness of internal control may vary over time.</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Because of the inherent limitations, any system of internal control over financial reporting, no matter how well designed, may not prevent or detect misstatements due to the possibility
                  that a control can be circumvented or overridden or that misstatements due to error or fraud may occur that are not detected.&#160; Also, projections of the effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal controls may
                  become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies and procedures included in such controls may deteriorate.</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Management has evaluated the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 based on the control criteria in the 2013 COSO Framework issued by the
                  Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&#160; Based on such evaluation, we have concluded that CTBI&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is effective as of December 31, 2025.</div>

                <div><br/>
                </div>

                <div style="text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The effectiveness of CTBI&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025 has been audited by BDO USA, P.C., an independent registered public accounting firm that
                  audited CTBI&#8217;s consolidated financial statements included in this annual report.</div>

                  Employee Stock Ownership Incentive Plan (&#8220;2025 Plan&#8221;) was approved by the Board of Directors and the Shareholders in 2024 and became active on February 1, 2025.&#160; The 2025 Plan had 550,000 shares authorized, all&#160;of which were available at
                  December 31, 2025.&#160; The 2015 Stock Ownership Incentive Plan (&#8220;2015 Plan&#8221;) was approved by the Board of Directors and the Shareholders in 2015.&#160; The 2015 Plan was rendered inactive as of February 1, 2025.&#160; Shares issuable pursuant to
                  awards which were granted under the 2015 Plan on or before their respective expiration or termination dates will be issued from the remaining shares reserved for issuance under the 2015 Plan.&#160; The shares of common stock reserved for
                  issuance under the 2015 Plan in excess of the number of shares as to which options or other benefits are awarded thereunder, and any shares as to which options or other benefits granted under the 2015 Plan may lapse, expire, terminate, or
                  be canceled, will not be reserved and available for issuance or reissuance under the 2025 Plan.</div>
